effect.label: What the workflow may do
effect.title: What the workflow may do, at every depth
effect.unknownEffect: Not computed yet. Every call computes it again before the start.
effect.scope: Counts everything inside: its agents and models, tools, result files, sub-workflows, teams and nested workflow tools. Every call computes it again, and the higher value counts.
effect.raised: It may do more now than when it was added. The call is asked with the current value.
effect.unknown: Unknown, counted as changing and external: {{items}}

approval.title: Start workflow “{{name}}”
approval.everyStart: A workflow that may change something is asked before every start. This decision holds for this start only and is not remembered.
approval.rejectHint: When rejected, the workflow does not start and the agent learns that it was refused. Without a decision, the start counts as rejected.

call.toolWaiting: A tool call of the workflow (“{{tool}}”) waits for approval.

updates.intro: A newer version exists for workflow tools of this agent. The agent keeps its fixed version until someone changes it:

section.title: Workflows as tools
section.off: Workflow tools are switched off here. This agent does not start while it has workflow tools: remove them, or ask your administrator to switch them on.
section.full: At most {{max}} workflow tools per agent.
section.hint: The agent can start a saved workflow in a fixed version and receives its result and files.

dialog.title: Add a workflow as a tool
dialog.description: The agent calls the workflow in the version you choose here. A newer version is only reported and never used by itself.
dialog.noVersions: This workflow has no saved version yet. Save it first.
dialog.versionHint: Fixed: the agent always calls this version.
dialog.blocked: This workflow needs files at its start ({{fields}}). A model cannot fill in file fields, so it cannot run as a tool.
dialog.asked: This workflow may change something: every start waits for approval in the conversation or the run.
